findings.summary: A sentence ROUND 2 ADDED is false in all three of its particulars: `GracefulReleaseMeterTest` contains no `T1` anywhere, the two `T1` mentions are in `GracefulReleaseMeter.java`, only one of them is javadoc, and they landed at M5.28 and M5.31 -- not M5.29. The tier correction it supports IS true; only its citation is wrong.
findings.detail: The added parenthetical reads: 'the tier (these cases build `MemoryBinStore`, which testing.md puts at T1 and this class's own javadoc has called T1 since M5.29)'. The class named two words earlier and holding 'these cases' is `GracefulReleaseMeterTest`. VERIFIED by grep on the staged tree and at HEAD: `grep -n 'T1\b' sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java` returns NOTHING in either. Every `T1` in this commit's surface is in the OTHER file, `GracefulReleaseMeter.java`: line 217 (staged) / 199 (HEAD), which IS javadoc, and HEAD line 94 ('caught only by the T1 case'), which is an INLINE COMMENT inside `observe` and is the line this commit deletes. Provenance, by `git log -S`: the inline one landed at `0e0db0f` M5.28, the javadoc one at `d48547a` M5.31. Neither is M5.29 (`6f1e724`). So the citation names the wrong class, the wrong comment kind for one of the two sites, and the wrong task. THE CONCLUSION IS STILL RIGHT and was verified independently: testing.md's tier table is 'T1 | component with fakes | `MemoryBinStore`', and all four new cases construct `new FaultInjectingStore(new MemoryBinStore(), ...)`, so T0 -> T1 is the correct correction. NOT BLOCKING: no test is weakened, the diff is comments-only outside the four added cases, and review.md rule 11 says fixing a minor opens a new prose surface -- this belongs in the commit body or a row rather than a round 3. EVERYTHING ELSE ROUND 2 ADDED WAS RE-MEASURED AND HOLDS. (1) Test bodies are byte-identical to round 1: the round-1 diff was reconstructed from its blobs and hashes to f66f9dae9da8 exactly, and the only test-file delta between rounds is one javadoc word, 'SURVIVED EVERY T0 CASE' -> 'SURVIVED EVERY CASE'. No assertion moved, none was weakened, `--numstat` is 184/0 on the test file and the meter delta is 100% comment lines. (2) All four kill claims re-measured in a throwaway worktree against a 501/0 baseline: `continue;`->`break;` reds ONLY `aPARTITIONRefusalAFTERANonPartitionFaultIsSTILLCounted`; deleting the `break` after `refusedForAnotherPod++` reds ONLY `TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce`; `int writesBefore = 0` reds ONLY `aSECONDWindowIsNotCreditedForTheFIRSTSWrite` with the sweep GREEN; `int before = 0` and `refusalsSeen = 0` each red exactly `refusalsACCUMULATEAcrossWindowsAndAreNotRECOUNTED` PLUS `CommitProtocolSweepTest.theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed` -- so the cell's 'is NOT their sole killer' is exact. (3) The round-2 comment's new named pair is exact: counting `refusalsSeen++` AFTER the carve-out reds `aRefusalBLAMINGANOTHERPODIsCountedAndTheReleaseIsNotCredited` AND `TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce` and nothing else, sweep green -- so the deleted 'caught only by the T1 case' was genuinely made false by this commit's second case. (4) The 38 sentence is true as narrowed: the sweep prints 'graceful releases 1608, refused for another pod 0, refusals seen 38', `CommitProtocolSweepTest:396` does assert `gracefulReleasesRefused` (accumulated from `run.gracefulReleasesRefusedForAnotherPod()`) `.isZero()`, and forcing the scan to stop at the first refusal per window still prints 38 -- MEASURED, both. (5) The narrowed `refusalsSeen()` javadoc matches the code and the two cases it cites: `TWORefusalsInOneWindowAreCountedTWICE` asserts 2 with `refusedForAnotherPod` zero, the new case asserts 1 for a window holding two. (6) The M5.57 row is accurate as my round-1 finding stated it: `refusedForAnotherPod++` -> `refusedForAnotherPod = 1` re-measured GREEN at 501/501 with the 1,000-seed sweep included; the two cases reaching that counter each run ONE window; the blindness reason it cites IS in `GracefulReleaseMeterTest`'s class javadoc verbatim ('On a correct tree refusedForAnotherPod is legitimately ZERO'); and its weaker-sibling note holds -- `released++` -> `released = 1` passes `aSECONDWindowIsNotCreditedForTheFIRSTSWrite` and reds `CommitProtocolSweepTest` alone.
findings.failure_scenario: A later author checks the tier claim the way the cell invites, greps `GracefulReleaseMeterTest` for `T1`, finds nothing, and concludes the cell's tier reasoning is unsupported -- or cites M5.29 as the commit that set a tier convention it never set, and carries that attribution into the next cell. This is the same 'a fix round writes a new false claim' pattern the round-1 findings were about, one layer down: the correction is right and its evidence is fabricated, which is harder to catch than a plain wrong claim because the conclusion checks out.
